# Animate list plugin: a measured row height, not a required itemHeight

## Context

The Institution's roster list rides `Neo.list.plugin.Animate` for its move/fade choreography and declares `itemHeight: 126` because the plugin refuses to run without one — the construct guard in `src/list/plugin/Animate.mjs`: *"list.plugin.Animate requires a fixed itemHeight and either a fixed itemWidth or the plugin-level minItemWidth"*. Dogfooding on the live fleet, 2026-09-12 (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#128): every card is 126 px tall for 78 px of content and the reserve reads as a gap. The consumer's only remedy is to hand-tune the constant to its composition, which cannot know how a long name wraps, what the font's metrics are, or whether a given record renders a second row. The operator challenged the constant: the plugin should become more flexible.

## The Problem

Height is the one geometry the plugin declares instead of measuring. Width is already measured: fluid mode (`minItemWidth_`) reads the owner's content rect on mount (`owner.getDomRect()` → `applyGeometry`) and on every ResizeObserver delivery (`onOwnerResize`), derives `columns` and writes `owner.itemWidth` back. Height has no such path: `applyGeometry` computes `rows = floor(rect.height / owner.itemHeight)`, `createItem` stamps `height: ${itemHeight}px` inline on every item node, and `getItemPosition` places row `r` at `r * (margin + itemHeight) + margin`. A consumer whose rows carry a variable number of lines either over-reserves (the roster) or clips.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Animate.mjs`: the construct guard; `applyGeometry(rect)` (fluid columns + `rows`); `onOwnerResize` (re-derive + reflow); `repositionItems` (one translate + width pass keyed by item id); `createItem` (inline height / position / transform / width, `null` before the first measurement); `getItemPosition`; the mount measurement through `owner.getDomRect()`; the filter/sort transition intercept (`transitionTimeoutId`).
- Consumers today: `src/menu/List.mjs`, `examples/dialog/*`, `examples/list/animate/List.mjs` (`itemHeight: 200`), the Institution roster (`itemHeight: 126`, `pluginAnimateConfig: {minItemWidth: 410}`). All fixed-height — the shipped mode stays the default.
- The measurement primitive exists: `owner.getDomRect()` / the main-thread rect read over item ids, batched; the plugin already owns one ResizeObserver registration for its owner.

## The Fix

An opt-in measured mode, symmetric to fluid width:

1. `itemHeight: null` on the owner plus the plugin's `measureItemHeight: true` lifts the height half of the construct guard; the guard's message names both admitted modes.
2. In measured mode `createItem` omits the inline `height` (an item stays as tall as its content) and, before the first measurement, renders the item hidden (`visibility: hidden` — there is no row to place it in yet); once the owner's settle pass fires (`createItems`, after its update resolved), the plugin measures the item rects in ONE batched DOM read (`owner.getDomRect(ids)`), takes the tallest as the uniform row height (a plugin-level `rowHeight`, guarded by `hasFixedItemHeight` the way `hasFixedItemWidth` guards width), re-derives `rows` and positions every item through `repositionItems`, which reveals them. No height is written back into the items: a written height is what the next measurement would read, so growth would go blind under `height` and shrink under `min-height` — rows are as tall as their tallest item, an item as tall as its content.
3. Measure again after an owner resize (once the fluid widths have landed — a width change changes wrapping), after a record change (the owner's `onStoreRecordChange` is wrapped the way `onStoreFilter` / `onStoreSort` are), and on every settle pass (`createItems` runs after load, sort and filter). An equal measurement repositions nothing. A font-load or theme delivery has no hook today and stays out of this ticket.
4. Stage two, its own ticket when wanted: variable row heights (each row as tall as its tallest member, `y` accumulating). The uniform measured row keeps the `index → (column, row)` math and the FLIP intercepts untouched, which is why it goes first.
5. Contract: the fixed mode (`itemHeight: Number`) is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixed mode unchanged: the existing plugin specs green without edits; `examples/list/animate` renders byte-identically; a fixed-mode consumer that changes `itemHeight` at runtime (126 → 200) keeps items and row geometry in step, as on dev.
- [ ] Measured mode: with `itemHeight: null` and measuring on, rows are as tall as the tallest rendered item; a record whose text wraps to a second line grows the row, as a reposition, not a rebuild.
- [ ] An owner resize that changes wrapping re-measures and repositions; an equal measurement repositions nothing (spy on `repositionItems`); a measurement overtaken by a newer read or by a mode switch publishes nothing when it lands.
- [ ] The filter/sort FLIP choreography is identical in both modes (no mode branch in the intercept path).
- [ ] A unit spec for the measured mode (the harness answers the rect read with fixed values) and a measured variant in `examples/list/animate`.
- [ ] Post-pin, in the Institution: the roster drops `itemHeight: 126` and its cards follow their composition (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#128, option a).

## Out of Scope

Masonry (per-column stacks — it changes reading order); variable per-row heights (stage two); the roster's surface and contrast choice (the Institution ticket's option c).

## Avoided Traps

- Measuring before the items have painted reads 0 — measure after the owner's update resolves, never inside `createItem`.
- Writing the measured height back into `owner.itemHeight` (the fluid-width precedent writes `itemWidth`) would make a fixed consumer indistinguishable from a measured one — keep the plugin-level `rowHeight` and the `hasFixedItemHeight` flag.
- Measurement loops: a reposition changes no item height, a font swap can — compare with the last measurement before repositioning.
- Writing the measured height back into the items (the first draft of Fix 2). The next measurement reads the written value: `height` blinds growth, `min-height` blinds shrink (a wider pane that unwraps the text would keep the old, taller rows — the #128 gap reappearing after a dock resize). The row height stays the plugin's number; a consumer that wants uniform card bottoms styles it.

Revised 2026-09-13 at implementation: Fix 2 / 3 lose the height write-back (a measured item stays its content's height, the first pass renders hidden, the settle pass is the trigger), the Contract Ledger names `rowHeight`, the guard and the `onStoreRecordChange` wrap, the trap above added. Revised at the first review (2026-09-14): `rowHeight` is a getter over the owner's live `itemHeight` in fixed mode and a plugin-owned `measuredRowHeight` in measured mode, and a measurement carries a request token — AC-1 / AC-3 and the ledger row widened.
